questions.q: According to the 2016 Standards, what is the Recommended Basic Fee (RBF) percentage for a Group 1 structure (simplest utilization of space) with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of Php 50M or less?
o: 10% of the PCC
7% of the PCC
3% of the PCC
5% of the PCC
questions.n: Group 1 structures, characterized by large open spaces and minimal complexity, start with a basic fee of 5%.

questions.q: If the architect only reaches the Design Development Phase (DDP) before the client cancels a Group 1 project with a BPF of Php 750,000.00, how much is the architect entitled to collect?
questions.n: By the end of Design Development, the architect is entitled to a cumulative total of 35% of the BPF.

questions.q: Which of the following building types are also classified under Group 1 (Simplest Utilization of Space)?
o: Libraries and Museums
Hangars, Freight Depots, and Packaging Plants
Hotels and Condominiums
Hospitals and Laboratories
questions.n: These structures typically involve large open spans and minimal interior detail, fitting the Group 1 definition.

questions.q: True or False: Interior Design services are already included in the 5% Basic Professional Fee for a Group 1 building.
o: False
True
questions.n: Interior Design is classified under SPP Doc 203 as a Specialized Architectural Service and is billed separately from regular services.

questions.q: According to Section 13 of RA 9266, what is the minimum weighted general average required to pass the Licensure Examination for Architects (LEA)?
o: 70%, with no grade lower than 50% in any given subject
Passing is based on a curve determined by the PRC
80%, with no grade lower than 70% in any subject
75%, with no grade lower than 60% in any subject
questions.n: This is the specific passing requirement mandated by law for architectural examinees.

questions.q: What is the 'Oath' required of every successful examinee before they can practice architecture?
o: The Oath of Allegiance to the Republic
The Oath of Secrecy regarding exam questions
The UAP Membership Oath
The Oath of Profession before the Board or authorized official
questions.n: Every professional must take this oath as a formal commitment to the ethics and standards of the architecture profession.

questions.q: Under Section 23 of RA 9266, what is a primary ground for the suspension or revocation of an architect's Certificate of Registration?
o: Unprofessional conduct or signing/sealing plans not prepared by the architect
Moving to a different city without notifying the Board
Failing to attend a UAP chapter meeting
Charging a fee higher than the RBF
questions.n: Signing 'dry' plans (plans not personally made or supervised) is a major legal violation.

questions.q: How many days after the date of the examination must the Board report the ratings obtained by each candidate to the Commission?
o: 60 days
Within 30 days
10 days
15 days
questions.n: The law provides 30 days for the board to finalize and report the examination results.

questions.q: What document is issued to an architect as evidence of their authority to practice after meeting all requirements?
o: Certified true copy of the LEA results
Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card
A notarized Service Agreement
A business permit from the DTI
questions.n: These documents, issued by the PRC, are the primary legal evidence of an architect's license.

questions.q: In the 'Architect's Responsibilities in Relation to his Client,' what is the rule regarding extra compensation from contractors?
o: The architect can accept a 'finder's fee' if the client is notified
The architect shall not accept any compensation from any person other than the Client
The architect can accept commissions if they are less than 2% of the material cost
The architect must split all commissions with the owner
questions.n: This ensures the architect remains an independent agent working solely in the interest of the client.

questions.q: What is the architect's duty to colleagues and subordinates regarding credit for work?
o: Credit is only given to those who are RLAs
The architect must give professional credit to those who contributed and not falsely claim authorship
The principal architect always takes 100% of the credit
Authorship is determined by whoever signs and seals the plans
questions.n: This fosters professional respect and ensures that subordinates' contributions are recognized for their own career growth.

questions.q: Under 'Relation to the Public,' what is the architect's stance on advertisements?
o: The architect should not use self-laudatory or misleading advertisements
Architects should use large billboards to gain visibility
Architects can claim to be the 'best in the country' in their ads
Advertising is strictly forbidden in all forms
questions.n: Professional listings and signs should be modest and factual to maintain the integrity of the profession.

questions.q: When an architect is asked to provide a 'Free Sketch' to a client to win a project, what does the Code of Ethics say?
o: Free sketches are a good way to demonstrate skill and build trust
The architect shall not render services without an agreement; free sketches are discouraged
Only interns are allowed to provide free sketches
Free sketches are allowed if the project cost is over Php 100M
questions.n: Professional services have value from the start; 'free' work undermines the standard of the profession.

questions.q: What is the architect's responsibility regarding Site Safety?
o: The architect must report observed unsafe conditions to the owner and contractor
The architect has no responsibility for safety whatsoever
The architect is solely responsible for all safety equipment
The architect must personally provide hard hats to all workers
questions.n: While the contractor manages safety, the architect has an ethical duty to flag dangers they encounter during visits.

questions.q: What is the 'Notice to Proceed' in a construction contract?
o: A permit issued by the Mayor's office
A notice that the contractor is being terminated
A written notice fixing the date on which construction work shall commence
A request for a change in design
questions.n: It is the formal 'green light' for the contractor to move on-site and start the contract time.

questions.q: What is a 'Change Order'?
o: A document used to hire a new subcontractor
A written order authorizing a change in work, price, or time
A notice from the bank regarding the project loan
An instruction to clean the construction site
questions.n: It is the legal mechanism for modifying the original contract scope or duration after work has begun.

questions.q: What is the 'Guarantee Bond' furnished by the contractor?
o: A bond to pay for the architect's insurance
A payment made to the architect for supervising the project
A bond that ensures the project is finished on time
A guarantee of the quality of materials and workmanship (usually for 1 year)
questions.n: This bond protects the owner from latent defects that appear shortly after completion.

questions.q: Who is primarily responsible for the payment of Building Permit fees?
o: The IAPOA
The Contractor
The Owner
The Architect
questions.n: As the ultimate beneficiary and property holder, the owner is responsible for all government-mandated permit fees.

questions.q: What is the 'Schedule of Materials and Finishes' in the context of contract documents?
o: A receipt from a hardware store
A detailed list of all materials and finishes to be used in the project
A timeline of when materials will arrive on site
A list of the workers' contact information
questions.n: This ensures the contractor knows exactly what brand, color, and type of materials are required by the architect.

questions.q: For a Group 5 (Monumental) project like a Museum, what is the Recommended Basic Fee (RBF) for the first unit?
o: 10% of the PCC
6% of the PCC
12% of the PCC
5% of the PCC
questions.n: Monumental structures require high levels of detail and specialized design, warranting a higher base fee.

questions.q: Calculate the BPF for the 1st Unit of a Museum with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of Php 45,000,000.00 (Group 5).
According to the 'Repetitive Construction' rule for specialized buildings (Group 5), what is the fee for the 2nd Unit?
questions.n: For the 2nd unit of a Group 5 project, the fee is 50% of the BPF of the 1st unit.
